rationale: Start with a broad mid-temperature scouting gradient to elute all 8 compounds and map the overall elution window without high risk of truncation. The wide phi range and moderate slope should reveal whether early peaks are unretained and whether late peaks need more strength or more time.

All peaks eluted between about phi_e 0.20 and 0.44, so narrowing the gradient window around the actual elution region should improve selectivity, especially for the unresolved 4/5 pair, while keeping all compounds inside the gradient. Keep tG and T fixed to isolate the effect of the phi window.

The narrowed window greatly improved the critical 4/5 pair, so now make the gradient shallower to test whether that pair is slope-responsive enough to cross R = 1.5. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed isolates slope effects on the only remaining weak pair.

The critical pair is strongly slope-responsive and is essentially at baseline at tG 30, so a slightly hotter run may keep it resolved while pulling t_last back toward 10 min. This tests whether temperature can recover time without sacrificing the 4/5 pair.

Lowering phi0 should give more space to the early-middle cluster that now contains the critical pairs, while a modestly shorter tG than 30 min aims to keep t_last closer to 10 min. Keep T at 40 C because 45 C changed selectivity unfavorably and shifted the worst pair.

We now have a fully resolved method, so the priority is cutting t_last toward 10 min while preserving resolution. A slightly stronger, steeper gradient should compress the run substantially from injection 5 yet likely retain enough margin because all pairs there were comfortably above 1.5.

Injection 6 over-compressed the chromatogram and created two failing pairs, so back off to a slightly shallower gradient while keeping the same window. This should recover resolution for the 4/5 and 6/7 pairs with only a modest increase in t_last.

The 6/7 pair is only slightly below baseline at tG 18, so one more step shallower with the same window should push it over R = 1.5. This is the most direct way to reach full resolution while staying close to the current best method.

Since tG 18 was near-optimal on resolution but penalized by t_last, increase phi1 one step to pull the late peaks earlier while keeping the same slope regime. This specifically targets the last cluster, including the formerly critical 6/7 pair, to see if time can be reduced without losing too much selectivity.

The best method so far is just short of full resolution, and changing phi1 upward hurt both critical pairs, so test temperature instead. Lowering T one step should modestly increase retention and potentially improve selectivity for the 6/7 pair while keeping the proven 0.20–0.50 window and tG 18 min.

The late pair appears highly sensitive to phi1, so lowering phi1 from 0.50 to 0.45 at the otherwise best tG should give the last cluster more gradient space and improve 6/7 resolution. Using tG 18 min keeps the run shorter than the fully resolved but slow 0.20–0.45, 24 min method.

The 0.20–0.45 window gives full resolution with large margins at tG 18, so the next move is to shorten tG aggressively and see how much time can be recovered before a pair drops below 1.5. This directly brackets the fastest acceptable fully resolved method in that favorable window.

At 0.20–0.45, tG 14 compressed the two critical pairs too much, while tG 18 had ample resolution but too much time penalty. Testing the midpoint tG 16 should balance those effects and may improve on the current best CRF.

The main challenge is balancing two different critical regions, so widening the window downward may spread the early-middle cluster while keeping phi1 at 0.50 to avoid the long t_last seen at phi1 0.45. This probes whether redistributing gradient space rather than only changing slope can outperform the current best.

At 0.20–0.50, tG 18 is very close to fully resolved and only loses on time, while 45 C previously altered selectivity enough to move the critical pair. Combining slightly shorter tG with higher T tests whether we can keep both critical pairs above 1.5 and pull t_last down toward 10 min.

Injection 15 is excellent on time but the 3/4 pair is now the only weak point, so make the gradient one step shallower while keeping the favorable high temperature. This should specifically improve 3/4 resolution with only a small time penalty and may surpass the current best CRF.

At 45 C the only weakness is the early-middle 3/4 pair, so raising phi0 should reallocate more of the gradient to that region without increasing t_last. Keep phi1, tG, and T fixed to target selectivity around the critical pair while preserving the excellent run time.

Raising phi0 worsened the late pair badly, so try the opposite direction from the current best: lower phi0 one step while keeping the same fast, high-temperature method. This may improve the 3/4 selectivity at 45 C without sacrificing the strong time advantage too much.

At 45 C the late pair is no longer limiting, so lowering phi1 one step from the best method may improve the early 3/4 selectivity while only modestly increasing t_last. This directly tests whether a slightly weaker upper endpoint can lift the sole sub-1.5 pair above threshold.

The best run is extremely close to ideal and only lacks a little 3/4 resolution; pushing both phi0 and phi1 upward preserves a similar slope and fast timing while shifting the gradient window to higher phi, where that pair may separate better. This is a targeted selectivity test around the current best high-temperature conditions.

We need to preserve the excellent speed of the 45 C, tG 16 method while trying to nudge the 3/4 pair upward; increasing only phi1 tests that specific selectivity shift without the severe late-pair collapse seen when phi0 was also raised. This is the cleanest remaining one-factor move around the current best conditions.

The 45 C, 16 min method is best because its tiny time penalty is outweighed by strong overall resolution, so the most promising remaining direction is to eliminate that penalty entirely with a shorter gradient. This tests whether t_last can be pushed under 10 min while retaining enough credit on the single weak 3/4 pair to beat the current best.

The unresolved pair at 45 C is consistently the early-middle 3/4 region, so shift the whole window upward one step while narrowing it to focus gradient time there. This sacrifices some margin on the late pair but is the most targeted remaining selectivity change to try to lift 3/4 without a time penalty.

Injection 23 is the best so far and only misses full credit on the 3/4 pair, so one step shallower is the most direct attempt to push that pair to R at or above 1.5. t_last is still below 10 min, leaving room for a modest increase in retention without incurring a time penalty unless it crosses 10.

The best method is already under 10 min but still slightly short on the 3/4 pair; making the gradient steeper will likely reduce that pair further, but this final run checks whether the gain from zero time penalty with an even shorter t_last can outweigh the small loss in pair credit. With only one injection left, this is the only nearby untested bracket around the best window and temperature.
